coachingPoints: Preparation starts before the catch — sprint your feet into position early.
Hop, don't run, into the shot; the two-foot hop is the fastest way to get square.
Your hands are a target — show the passer a big, ready chest with hands up.
Beat the ball with your feet: be shot-ready before the pass arrives, not after.
Film yourself: most players discover their 'hop' is actually a slow two-step.
commonMistakes: Standing flat-footed and catching, then starting the footwork — fix: move during the pass, not after it.
Running through the catch off-balance — fix: replace the run with a hop that lands you square.
Catching with hands down — fix: hands chest-high, presenting a target on every catch.
Only preparing for catch-and-shoot — fix: use the same hop to prepare drives and one-dribble pull-ups.
description: Get your feet, hands, and body ready before the ball arrives — the hidden half of every great jumper.
gameSituations: Catch-and-shoot threes — the entire shot is decided by what your feet did before the catch.
Coming off screens — sprint, hop into the catch, and be ready to shoot or drive instantly.
Transition trail shots — the trailer who hops into the catch shoots before the defense sets.

howTo.detail: As the pass leaves the passer's hands, move your feet toward the spot. Great shooters arrive before the ball; average shooters arrive with it.
howTo.title: Move before the catch

howTo.detail: Finish your movement with a small two-foot hop that lands you balanced, knees bent, facing the basket. The hop kills your momentum and sets your base in one move.
howTo.title: Hop into a balanced base

howTo.detail: Show the passer both hands at chest height, fingers up. A ready target means a cleaner catch and a faster release.
howTo.title: Present your hands early

howTo.detail: Catch the ball already in your shooting pocket position — up near the chest/forehead, not down at your waist. Less travel means a quicker shot.
howTo.title: Catch high and ready

howTo.detail: Be in a position to shoot, drive, or pass the instant the ball touches your hands. Preparation is not just for shooting — it is for every decision.
howTo.title: Decide from a ready stance

title: Shot Preparation
whatIsIt: Shot preparation is everything you do before the ball reaches you: how your feet move, where your hands are, and how your body arrives balanced and facing the basket. Most players think shooting starts at the catch. Elite shooters know it starts two seconds earlier.

The difference is measured in tenths of a second. A shooter who hops into a ready stance before the catch can release in under 0.6 seconds. A shooter who starts moving after the catch needs twice as long — and by then, the defender has arrived.
whyItMatters: Defense closes out at sprint speed, so shooting is a race against the closeout. Preparation is how you win that race without rushing your mechanics. It is also the most coachable shooting skill: you cannot grow taller or jump higher, but you can absolutely learn to move your feet before the catch. Teams that teach preparation see their whole roster shoot faster and better.
